steps.text: Mix cooking wine, soy sauce, vinegar, oil, and garlic together in the bottom of a baking dish. Place mushroom caps into the baking dish with the gills facing up. Spoon marinade into the cavities, cover with foil, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes. Flip mushrooms and bake until mushrooms are tender and juicy, about 8 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Savannah’s Best Marinated Portobello Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Marinate portobello mushroom caps for 15 minutes with a mixture of garlic, balsamic vinegar, and soy so they’ll be just the right texture after cooking.
raw_recipe.name: Savannah’s Best Marinated Portobello Mushrooms

review.reviewBody: I wound up making a couple small modifications to this. I didn't have cooking wine nor did I have fresh garlic. I omitted the wine and subbed 1/4 tsp garlic salt for each clove. It was easy and worked out to be rather tasty. I'll happily make this one again.

This has become one of my family's favorite recipes! I roast red peppers at the same time, and a few minutes before the mushrooms finish up, I add the red peppers and fresh mozzarella for just enough time to melt. Top with fresh basil! Served with cauliflower rice, it makes a great meatless meal!

This is a great base recipe I use for portobellos. I’ve made it about a dozen times either grilled or roasted. It always turns out great as long as I don’t stray too far from the original recipe. I tend to use Marsala cooking wine, add lemon juice, black pepper, red pepper flakes, and tend to marinate it for at least 4 hours. Keep this recipe handy if you have people over that might have alternative diets, they’ll thank you for it and you’ll enjoy it too!!

Delicious as a burger! A lot of marinades tend to use so much vinegar it becomes all you can taste. The wine provided a nice balance. I marinated whole caps (using a nice Merlot in place of cooking wine). I also used Tamari in place of Soy - probably not a big difference but it was all I had. All the ingredients were whisked together in a measuring cup and poured inside of the caps. After a while I flipped them briefly to get a little of the marinade on the outside as well.

I then grilled the caps with a sprinkling of Gorgonzola, and served them up on a hard roll. My boyfriend had only had portobellos once before and had not been sold on them then. With this recipe he could not stop raving about how delicious they were, "...better than steak" were his exact words.

You need something to take the edge off the balsamic vinegar. I added a tbsp of maple syrup, a tsp of kosher salt, a dash of pepper, and subbed rice wine vinegar for the cooking wine... it's really, really tasty!

This recipe is GREAT and I'm going to agree with earlier reviews (thank you, btw) because the 1 tbl spoon of balsamic and a regular wine went a long way! We also added a teaspoon of mustard and used BRAGGS instead of soy sauce for the marinade ;-)

After they were cooked we put a little white/fresco crumbly cheese which we sprinkled with dried rosemary, a bit of comte and a dash of asiago. We broiled it to brown the cheese and then made it into a sandwich! It was "mmmm" in every bite!

This was delish!! I used 1/4c cooking sherry in place of the wine and doubled the garlic. I also cut the mushroom before marinating/baking. Served over mixed green salad and used the liquid and garlic as the "dressing" it was so good!

Ever since I found this recipe I've used it as my go to for a portobello mushroom marinade. I make the recipe mostly as is, here are my changes:
1. Use red cooking wine, doesn't say which to use, or can use whatever red wine is on hand at the time. 
2. Minced garlic, the one found near the produce not dried, vs garlic clove. 
3. Then I add a some water to make more liquidy. 
4. If needed I add a little more of stuff like garlic or vinegar to taste. 
5. Place the mushrooms stem side up and spoon some liquid into the cap and let sit. Remove stem if grilling and marinade as well. 
We prefer to grill them, so this works better for us and is still very flavorful!

Use regular red wine in place of cooking wine and it's a winner. I personally throw some red peppers into the marinade and remove them before cooking then saute them before the mushrooms are done. Throw it on some focaccia with greens and you've got a winner.

These were decadent! I had no wine--it never gets saved for cooking ;)--but I replaced it with chianti vinegar, which was very suitable. I doubled the garlic and crushed the cloves to release more flavour. I also added a generous amount of fresh ground pepper and basil. I sauted them until soft, and the skillet captured all of the mushrooms' savoury juices, blending them with the other flavours. Delicious! What a perfect complement to beef!!!

I loved this! Super easy and they were so juicy! My only suggestions (and what I did) are to definitely use a wine that you'd drink and a quality aged balsamic for richness. I'll be making these again and again for sure!
i like balsamic vinegar but not on this, not terrible though.

One of my favorite things about this website is reading the comments people thoughtfully leave. This recipe probably was excellent as originally written, but reading comments from people who added Worcestershire made me add some since I love that stuff! This was one of the best portobello recipes I've ever tried. I cut up the mushrooms after cooking and added them, and the leftover juices, to my pasta sauce with other fresh sauteed veggies. It took the sauce to another level, made it one of the best meals ever!
So easy, quick & delicious! Made this recipe countless times. A winner!
I have done this recipe so many times. I cannot get tired of it!
Quick and easy to get ready for baking. I've been used to pan saute and am looking forward to this new method for me. Thanks
I used cranberry juice instead of cooking wine.

I used a nice red wine instead of cooking wine, and I doubled the recipe for 4 mushrooms except for the soy sauce and vinegar ( I used 1.5 the amount and recommend reduced sodium soy sauce as it was a bit salty) It was great!
I made this with red wine and did not like it as much as a grilled mushroom recipe that I made last weekend that had simply garlic, soy sauce and onion.
